summary: Invalid fixed-instance all-time lower-bound proof; not a disproof of the positive-curvature results

problems.title: Fixed-instance all-time lower-bound proof fails for its proposed finite-dimensional witness
problems.source_claim_location: Theorem 3.2 p.5 Eq.(11); Appendix F p.18 Eq.(48); Section 2.2 p.4

problems.impact: Invalid proof of claimed all-time nonconvergence used for necessity characterization; full theorem under any alternate existential interpretation not disproved

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed physical pp.3,5,18: Definitions 2.1-2.2, Assumptions 2.3-2.5, Definition 3.1 memory/output, Theorem 3.2 quantifiers and Eq.(11), Appendix F Eq.(48) and its asserted attained minimizer. Read physical p.4 Section 2.2 dependency.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: The whole-family argument uses finite dimension, convex Lx-smooth h and attainment as explicitly asserted for Eq.(48). Delta_x=0 is a declared lower bound, not a requirement that the maximal curvature modulus vanish. The m=20 illustration has Lx=4>0, Ly=2>mu_y=1, Lxy=2>mu_yx=1, mu_xy=0; range and singular-value clauses of Assumption 2.5 are satisfied.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: At v=y=0 the full primal gradient preserves the u block and zero other blocks, so step 1/Lx is in Definition 3.1 gradient memory and uses finite time. Cocoercivity gives d_next^2 <= d^2-||grad h||^2/Lx^2 for each minimizer. Boundedness, gradient decay and finite-dimensional subsequence compactness give a minimizing cluster point; Fejer monotonicity relative to that point yields full convergence and eventual violation of any positive distance floor. Recomputed chain diagnostic using the closed form H^-1 e1 (no linear solver or author code) gives first crossing k=148.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: For each horizon a different dimension and hard function can give a valid worst-case lower bound. That is not the printed existence-before-all-times assertion. A single strongly convex member does not by itself refute the existential theorem; the general convergence argument defeats the entire proposed attained finite-dimensional witness family.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for Appendix F supporting the core negative claim invoked by Section 2.2. Does not establish failure of Theorem 3.3, all positive-curvature guarantees, or every possible construction satisfying only Assumptions 2.3-2.5.
independent_check.repair_scope: A horizon-dependent formulation is plausible but requires a fresh statement and proof with dimension, oracle costs and epsilon quantifiers. No fully repaired theorem is certified.

limitations: Long H-J and K.1.1 proofs not independently verified
